statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and Regimparc/Infogreffe availability search via infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate name must be capable of clear transcription in French-language Latin script; Article 5 of Décret n° 2014-1317 (loi Toubon) applies to statutory publications and RCS filings. Non-French words are permitted only when accompanied by a French transliteration and must not render the name confusing as to legal form or nationality.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the INPI registrar or by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce attached to the chosen RCS, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the President of the Tribunal judiciaire (commercial chamber) within one month of notification (Article R. 123-90 Code de commerce). Alternatively, the applicant may immediately file a revised name application via the formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr portal. No fee is assessed for the administrative appeal; the applicant must employ an avocat to engage the court route.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual and domiciliation offices are generally permitted for a SARL operating a low-risk cybersecurity SaaS, provided the registered office is a physical address in France capable of receiving service of process, administrative notices, and the statutory publication obligations. A domiciliation agreement (convention de domiciliation) is required, and for service companies, domiciliation at a domiciliation entreprise is accepted for no more than 5 years unless the company subsequently establishes its own commercial premises (Article L. 123-11-1 Code de commerce).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical on-site inspection risk is quantified as low-to-moderate at approximately 5% per year for a domestic-registered cybersecurity SaaS entity; the probability increases to 10% if the entity becomes VAT-exempt, files irregular payroll, or is flagged by FICUS/FICOBA data anomalies. For pure digital SaaS with no stock inventories, the inspection focus will be on substance indicators: leases, board minutes, operational management presence, and AML records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) of the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; online professional portal: impots.gouv.fr (Gestion et consultations via 'Espace Professionnel'), with company formalities handled through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporation of the SARL via the Guichet Unique (guichet-entreprises) triggers issuance of the SIREN/SIRET (French business identifiers) by INSEE. Step 2: VAT registration (TVA intracommunautaire number) is obtained by filing the standardized DGFiP notice of VAT commencement (form/declaration under Article 286-ter of the CGI) either through the Guichet Unique or directly with the local DGFiP Business Registration Service (SIAV – Service de l'Immatriculation des Assujettis à la TVA). Step 3: Foreign-established entities selling electronically supplied services into France may alternatively register under the Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) for B2C supplies or the reverse-charge mechanism for B2B supplies, avoiding a full French fixed-establishment VAT profile; a physical French establishment, such as a SARL branch, mandates full local VAT registration and issuance of a FR+ identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: By default, a SARL (other than a societe unipersonnelle SARL) is subject to Corporation Tax (impôt sur les sociétés – IS) on its worldwide-deemed French-source taxable income at the rate of 25% (reduced rate 15% on profits up to EUR 42,500 under conditions). It may elect, under Article 206-3 CGI, pass-through taxation (régime des sociétés de personnes / impôt sur le revenu – IR) only if strictly constituted as a family or small SME enterprise (limited to 50 employees and EUR 10 million turnover). No direct 'check-the-box' election exists; instead, companies choose taxation status at formation/amendment through the Guichet Unique and, once taxed as IR, must obtain DGFiP consent to switch back to IS. Hybrid mismatch elections are constrained by the EU ATAD/ATAD2 rules transposed into the French CGI (Articles 212-1 bis and following), which neutralize double-deduction and deduction-without-inclusion outcomes; election must be documented with a compliant GAAP/French accounting basis and prior-year permanent files.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) – French VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For French-established taxable persons: mandatory registration upon incorporation regardless of turnover (no economic threshold; the EUR 85,000 / EUR 37,500 'franchise en base' derogations exempt small micro-businesses from collection, not from registration eligibility for cross-border activities). For non-established foreign suppliers of electronically supplied services (SaaS): a EUR 10,000 Union-wide annual distance-sales threshold triggers French VAT registration or OSS filing; for B2B supplies, the domestic reverse-charge mechanism eliminates any French VAT registration requirement, whereas a fixed establishment in France (e.g., SARL) eliminates the EUR 10,000 threshold and imposes full registration from the first taxable transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing (facturation électronique) schedule under the 2026–2027 reform: mandatory issuance and transmission of e-invoices between taxable persons (B2B) and platform-based e-reporting of cross-border transactions, phased for large and mid-size enterprises from 1 September 2026 and for SMEs/micro-businesses from 1 September 2027. All invoices must pass through an authorized Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the State Public Platform (PPF) using EN 16931 semantic standards (Factur-X/UBL/CII), with real-time transmission of transaction data to DGFiP through open APIs; the XML e-invoice must include VAT identification numbers, taxable base, and applicable VAT rate. Although France does not operate a real-time fiscal 'stamping' or clearance center, the new architecture imposes continuous API-driven data flow and fraud analytics; failure to transmit the e-invoice within one business day after issuance exposes the taxpayer to administrative fine of EUR 15 per invoice (EUR 250 per invoice for tampering) and loss of deduction rights.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 262-I-1° CGI, exports of goods to destinations outside the European Union are zero-rated (TVA exonérée avec droit à déduction) provided that the goods physically leave the EU Customs Territory and the transport is evidenced. Exported services (e.g., cybersecurity SaaS, cloud vulnerability scanning, penetration testing) supplied to a non-EU customer follow the place-of-supply rule of Article 259-1 CGI: B2B supplies to non-established customers are deemed to take place outside France and are outside the scope of French VAT (not technically 0% but fully non-taxable with a right to recover input VAT on directly attributable costs); B2C supplies of electronically supplied services to non-EU customers are likewise outside scope. For exports of hardware/on-premises security appliances, the 0% rate applies only where the exporter (or its client) proves the physical transfer of goods out of the EU; provision of services auxiliary to the export (e.g., logistics, implementation) also qualifies under Article 262-I-2° CGI. The taxpayer must maintain a robust documentary file demonstrating the destination, transport route, incoterms, and delivery against purchase orders.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged via DELTA-X (N° EX1) within the French customs single window
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing physical departure from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank SWIFT/MT103 proof of consideration received in convertible currency for exported sales
Commercial invoice in English/French stating incoterms, HS classification, and value
Packing list and inward/outward transport document (CMR or maritime/air cargo manifest)
CE marking certificate or Euro-1/form EUR.1 where preferential tariff treatment is claimed
Export delivery receipt signed by the non-EU buyer or its customs broker
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Exported zero-rating claims are subject to rigorous DGFiP post-clearance audits: where supporting transport documents are missing or inconsistent, or where the buyer or goods are subsequently found to have re-entered France, the 0% rate is retroactively reversed and VAT is assessed at 20% with application of intérêt de retard (statutory interest, currently 0.55% per month) and the 40% / 80% 'manquement délibéré' / 'abus de droit' penalty surcharge (étendue des pénalités of Articles 1728–1729 CGI) on understated VAT; in qualified fraud, up to 100% surcharge and criminal fines under Article 1741 CGI (max EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment for senior officers for tax evasion) may apply. For exchange-control purposes, export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated to France within 180 days; unjustified non-repatriation triggers customs penalty of up to 5% of the outstanding amount under the French Customs Code (Code des douanes, Articles 413-5 and 459), with the buyer's payment receipts scrutinized as part of the economic substance test under ATAD.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), with prudential supervision delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), operating within the European System of Central Banks and under the legal framework of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier) and EU Capital Movements Regulation (Article 63 TFEU).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full current and capital account convertibility for EUR-denominated and cross-border transactions. Capital movements are fully liberalized under EU law, subject only to general derogations for public policy, national security, and EU sanctions. Profit remittance (dividend distribution, repayment of shareholder loans, royalty and service payments) is lawful without prior foreign exchange authorization, but is subject to French corporate withholding tax on outbound dividends (generally 25% or 5% under a tax treaty), transfer pricing documentation requirements, and mandatory reporting to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics (tableau de bord). The euro is freely convertible in both current and capital accounts; there are no exchange control barriers, surrender requirements, or bi-lateral clearing restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio to EUR. Exporters may retain balances in foreign currencies in authorized foreign currency accounts; however, all receipts must be booked in EUR for statutory accounting purposes under Article L.123-22 of the French Commercial Code, and all cross-border transactions exceeding EUR 12,500 must be reported to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments compilation. Payment instructions for export settlements must satisfy EU Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds, including full originator and beneficiary identification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with legal constraints. Regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions (PIs) authorized by the ACPR or passporting into France under PSD2 may open French IBAN accounts and provide treasury clearing services for cybersecurity SaaS receivables. Well-capitalized EMIs such as Qonto, Shine, or Currencycloud-backed platforms are viable for low-risk operational collections and cross-border vendor payments. However, EMIs cannot provide credit, deposit products, or documentary letters of credit; they are unsuitable as capital escrow banks for the legal share capital of an SARL, which must be held with a credit institution licensed under Article L.511-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. Offshore EMIs are subject to French AML/KYC transfer-of-funds rules and are legally less defensible for high-ticket contract escrow and parent-subsidiary cash pooling.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law (Articles L.561-4 to L.561-14 of the French Monetary and Financial Code) does not impose an absolute statutory mandate of physical presence for company directors during KYC onboarding. Remote onboarding is permitted via ANSSI-certified eIDAS video-identification and qualified electronic signatures, provided the bank applies equivalent due diligence measures to those OCCAM-compliant procedures. Many traditional French banks internally require a physical interview or authenticated video conference with the legal representative(s), production of original corporate documents, and verification of the beneficial owner's identity. For a foreign-owned SARL, a branch visit in Paris, Lyon, or Aix-en-Provence is generally required only where the company lacks a listed French director or where the bank's AML risk appetite triggers enhanced due diligence; remote opening with a sworn notarized apostille dossier is accepted by digital-first banks but is commercially rejected by tier-1 universal banks for capital escrow accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity for a non-resident parent company owning the SARL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry extract (Kbis) of the parent, notarized certificate of ultimate beneficial owners (attestation des bénéficiaires effectifs), grandparent corporate structure chart, directors' passport copies, utility or bank statements confirming residential address of all UBOs, and a signed declaration of source of wealth for the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure or PEP status of directors/UBOs or negative media screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party sanctions screening report against EU, OFAC, ONS, and UN lists dated within 30 days; professional reference letters from a regulated EU financial institution or licensed attorney; a Korean-level adverse-media report with negative results; PEP self-declaration form and high-risk-country business rationale if mathematically required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear economic rationale of fund flows for cross-border SaaS sub-licensing and cybersecurity service provision
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed customer contracts, down-stream sub-license agreements, an organizational chart showing substance of French operations, employment contracts in France, commercial invoices with ISIC 6201 description, and a transfer pricing benchmarking memo showing arm's length remuneration for the French entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient documentation of the source of funds for the SARL's initial share capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate board resolution approving the capital call, notarized bank transfer statements from the parent's bank with SWIFT MT103 reference, parent company audited financial statements, a source-of-wealth statement for the shareholder, and legal ownership deed of any inherited asset used for funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse flag due to invoicing or receipts from high-risk end-customers or partially disclosed downstream payment flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) policy including customer KYC due diligence procedures, transaction monitoring protocols, sanctions-screening software evidence, a register of all material end-customers, and a sworn compliance attestation from the French statutory auditor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for non-resident shareholder capital injection: a SWIFT MT103 instructed by the parent company's bank to the SARL's designated EUR account at a French credit institution. The payment purpose field (PURP code) must use ISO 20022 category 'INVP' with appropriate narrative 'Capital subscription to SARL' or the mutual partner's code
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.corresponding: La Banque de France mandates balance-of-payments reporting with code 'E51 – Capital contributions' (investissements directs) within 20 business days. The bank will require a shareholder resolution (extrait de procès-verbal d'assemblée), a capital subscription statement (bulletin de souscription), and an updated Kbis from the registry within one month. For a SARL with non-resident corporate shareholders, the inbound telex should also present the balance-of-payments declaration form (FEBNRF) or the bank's electronic annex for inward direct investment; verification of the registered share capital is performed by the notary or the bank upon final blocking of share capital in escrow.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) For EU vendor payments and subscription royalties: SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or SEPA Instant is the standard rail with IBANs; (2) For non-EU supplier disbursements: SWIFT MT103 with mandatory beneficiary details and purpose code
See  chapter  on  permissible  FX  hedging  instruments  and  the  rules  for  CD  -
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.commercial: For high-value infrastructure purchases where LC is required: irrevocable documentary letter of credit (MT700) issued by a French bank in favour of the software/data-centre vendor, payable against shipping and acceptance documents; (3) For outbound trade-payments for services, mandatory ISO 20022 purpose code 'TRADE' or 'SERV' with the contract number; (4) For intra-group management fees or royalties, the French treasury must withhold the applicable withholding tax and ensure that the payment instruction encodes transfer-pricing documentation with the invoice, tax certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale), and signed intercompany agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla EUR/USD forward contracts (promptes) with a licensed French bank under the French Money and Financial Code and EMIR regulations
Cross-currency swaps (devises) for fixed- or floating-rate conversion between EUR and USD/CAD, subject to ISDA Master Agreement and CSA collateral requirements

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) with a licensed credit institution for emerging-market high-risk currencies (e.g., TWD, KRW, PLN) for receivable protection, permitted under French prudent derivative rules only where the underlying exposure is economically justified and the contract is booked at arm's length
Currency-options (cap/floor strategies) for hedging group-company payable exposure where permitted by the French bank's derivative acceptance policy for small-cap treasury clients

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard CIT rate applicable to all taxable profits for fiscal years commencing on or after 1 January 2022)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit per fiscal year for eligible SME/SARL satisfying all conditions of Article 219-I-b CGI (net turnover < EUR 10 million; share capital fully paid up; at least 75% of capital held by individuals); Research Tax Credit (Crédit d'Impôt Recherche) at 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% of defined innovation-protection expenditure; reduced 15% rate on qualified long-term capital gains from certain patent disposals.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_rule: Unlimited carry-forward period under Article 209 CGI, but each year's deduction is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000; optional carry-back of losses to the immediately preceding three years, limited to EUR 1,000,000 and refundable or creditable after five years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (annual corporate income tax return, 'Liasse Fiscale') with the 2050-series annexes (2050 to 2059-F), filed electronically via the DGFiP EDI-TDFC/EFI e-filing portal on impots.gouv.fr; electronic filing is mandatory for all SARLs.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (once per fiscal year); CIT instalment payments are made quarterly on Form 2571-SD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of fiscal year-end. For a SARL with a 31 December fiscal year-end, the online filing deadline is the second business day following 1 May of the next year (e.g., 31 December 2024 year-end due on 3 May 2025); paper filing deadline is the first business day after 1 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SARL's French SIREN, SIRET, fiscal domicile, activity code (NAF 6201Z for ISIC 6201) and intra-Community VAT number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only the SARL's own French identifiers; foreign parent or shareholder identifiers are not entered on this frame. Cross-border related-party transactions are declared separately in Annex Form 2257.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss after reconciliation of the accounting result with tax law: reintegration of non-deductible expenses (e.g., 50% of business entertainment and certain fines) and deduction of prior-year loss carry-forwards and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL is taxed at entity level in France; treaty residence of the shareholders does not modify the computation of the SARL's French taxable base. The SARL remains subject to French CIT on worldwide profits unless the foreign parent's PE exception applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the share of taxable profit eligible for the reduced 15% SME rate up to the EUR 42,500 ceiling; the excess is taxed at the standard 25% rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the shareholding test: the reduced rate is denied if more than 25% of the SARL's capital is held by a legal entity. If a foreign parent corporation holds a controlling interest, the full 25% standard rate applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of loss carry-forwards deducted in the current year, computed under the EUR 1,000,000 plus 50%-of-excess annual cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a detailed schedule of the loss history and the computation of the capped deduction; no foreign approval is required, but the documentation must be retained for six years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex 2059-A — Box CIR/CII (Research and Innovation Tax Credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the Crédit d'Impôt Recherche at 30% of eligible R&D salaries, depreciation and subcontracting up to EUR 100 million; separate computation of Crédit d'Impôt Innovation at 20% up to EUR 400,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only French-established R&D performing activities within the SARL and the French tax territory qualify; outsourcing to foreign affiliates must be declared and is generally excluded unless the foreign subcontractor is a French PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file: 5% of the assessed tax due under Article 1728 CGI, increased to 10% after formal notice ('mise en demeure'), 40% for concealed activities, and 80% for fraudulent behaviour or abuse of law; late payment interest of 0.20% per month under Article 1727 CGI; non-electronic filing incurs a specific fine of EUR 150 per form (minimum EUR 60).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571-SD (Acompte d'Impôt sur les Sociétés) filed via the same mandatory DGFiP EFI/EDI-TDFC electronic portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (four instalments during the current tax year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December of the tax year; any balance payable or recoverable is settled with the annual Form 2065-SD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A — Base de l'acompte (Instalment Base)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated taxable profit for the current fiscal year after deduction of the prior year's accumulated CIT instalments; the reduced-rate share is computed separately.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute on the same entity-level French result as the annual return; instalments cannot be reduced merely because the parent resides abroad unless treaty relief has been formally granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of CIT prepayments, research tax credit and any withheld tax credits available against instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits attributable to a foreign branch of the SARL may be offset only to the extent provided by the applicable DTA; the underpaid balance attracts interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Unpaid or under-paid instalment: late penalty of 5% of the missing amount plus monthly interest at 0.20%; the French administration may automatically assess the estimated instalment basis if no return is filed by 1 December.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Article 119 bis-2 CGI on gross dividends paid by the French SARL to a non-resident shareholder; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Article 119 ter CGI) when the parent is an EU/EEA company holding at least 5% of the SARL for an uninterrupted two-year period; DTA-reduced rates commonly range from 0% to 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Prior to distribution, the foreign shareholder must provide the SARL with a valid Certificate of Residence (Formulaire 5000) issued by the competent foreign tax authority; for relief at source, Form 5001 may be filed supported by the DTA schedule and, where applicable, a two-year holding attestation. Approved claims are applied at the moment of distribution; where relief has been denied at source, the shareholder may file a refund claim ('réclamation contentieuse') with the DGFiP within two years of the levy. The SARL must retain the TRC, the shareholding/parking proof and the minutes of the general assembly declaring the dividend for six years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and licence fees paid by the French SARL to non-residents are subject to a statutory withholding tax of 33.33% under Article 182 B CGI where the rights are exploited in France; the EU Interest & Royalties Directive may reduce this to 0% for associated EU companies subject to a 25% threshold; relevant DTA rates are typically 0%-10% for patents and 5%-10% for software licences. Statutory withholding tax on arm's-length interest is generally 0% under Article 131 quater CGI for conventional loans, provided the lender has no French PE; interest paid to a shareholder whose current-account advances exceed reasonable limits may be recharacterised as profit distributions, triggering the 25% dividend WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: France imposes no general Local File/Master File obligation on a SARL of this size; mandatory full TP documentation applies to entities exceeding EUR 400,000,000 annual turnover or EUR 2,000,000,000 balance-sheet total. However, the SARL must pre-comply with Article L.13 AA/AB LPF and Annual Form 2257-SD whenever cumulative intra-group transactions with foreign related companies exceed EUR 200,000 per year, requiring a concise arm's-length report and contemporaneous evidence.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not administer a standalone 'ESR Certificate' regime in the style of the UAE; economic substance is enforced through the general abuse-of-law doctrine (Article L.64 LPF), the French CFC rules (Article 209 B/CGI), and the 'effective management seat' requirement. The SARL must maintain genuine local substance: French registered office, board/gérant decisions taken in France, French payroll with operating personnel, local servers or documentation, and commercial contracts negotiated in France. A purely circular arrangement involving a foreign shell subcontractor with no employees, premises or decision-making autonomy is vulnerable to CIT recharacterisation and 80% 'abus de droit' penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion — Deliberate Concealment of French CIT/VAT Base (Fraude Fiscale)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of French SaaS and penetration-testing revenue through an undeclared foreign payment account (e.g., foreign Stripe/currency accounts) or issuing sham invoices to a related shell entity to strip taxable profits from the SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full French tax base plus a 40% or 80% penalty under Article 1729 CGI and monthly 0.20% late-payment interest; criminal conviction under Article 1741 CGI carries imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, increased to up to seven years and EUR 2,000,000 where the fraud involves organised crime or cross-border concealment; aggravated sanctions include confiscation of the concealed assets, publication of the judgment, and suspension of professional licences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant (manager) may be held jointly and severally liable for the SARL's unpaid taxes under Article 267 LPF; criminal conviction of the gérant applies for signing fraudulent declarations. The corporate veil may be pierced via 'gestion de fait' where a foreign controlling shareholder exercises real management without formal office; civil restitution, travel bans and imprisonment follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Shell Conduit Characterisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying above-market commissions to an affiliated foreign subcontractor that holds no independent assets, personnel, technical capacity or decision-making substance, while failing to file Form 2257 and contemporaneous arm's-length documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT adjustment reallocating the full margin to the SARL, plus a 40% deliberate-misstatement penalty under Article 1729 CGI; failure to produce TP documentation in response to a formal notice carries a EUR 15,000 fine under Article L.13 AA LPF; payments to a non-cooperative jurisdiction may be disallowed with a 75% final withholding penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who executes the non-arm's-length contracts exposes personal assets to civil liability for management fault under Article L.223-22 of the French Commercial Code; an 'abus de biens sociaux' finding (Article L.241-3) triggers five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with the tax judge empowered to disregard the SARL's separate legal personality as a sham conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Concealment of Digital-Asset Receipts (AML)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting payment for penetration-testing or vulnerability SaaS subscriptions through crypto-wallet laundering chains or offshore payment processors, deliberately obscuring the beneficial owner, or failing to make the mandatory Tracfin suspicious-transaction report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 324-1 of the French Penal Code: simple money laundering carries five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine; aggravated laundering (habitual, professional, or organised) carries ten years' imprisonment and a EUR 750,000 fine; the SARL as a corporate entity is exposed to a fine five times the statutory maximum (up to EUR 1,875,000 to EUR 3,750,000) together with confiscation of the connected cryptocurrency and real-estate assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who structures, converts or transfers tainted cryptocurrency assets is subject to the same criminal penalties personally; a travel ban, freezing of personal bank accounts, and confiscation of personal property are available. The AML compliance officer's personal criminal liability is engaged for deliberate failure to declare suspicious cross-border transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illicit Dividend Repatriation — Withholding Tax Evasion on Profit Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to a non-resident shareholder without withholding the statutory 25% tax, or improperly applying the 0% EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive before the two-year holding period has elapsed or without a valid certificate of residence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SARL is liable as withholding agent for the entire un-withheld amount, plus a 5%-10% late-filing penalty and 0.20% monthly interest under Articles 1728 and 1731 CGI; if the arrangement is characterised as tax evasion, an 80% penalty applies and the shareholders' personal tax position is reassessed in France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who signs the dividend distribution knowingly without WHT becomes personally liable for the corporate WHT debt; presence of fraudulent intent leads to criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI, restrictions on leaving France while the debt subsists, and disqualification from corporate management.
